passage:
9 November.
Mohit was late today. Twenty minutes. Old me would have spiralled: he's bored of me, he's found someone better, typical. I felt it start, that cold drop. Then I remembered the last eight months. Every Sunday he has turned up. When he can't, he texts. Once he rode across Pune in the rain because I panicked about my scholarship. So I wrote on my hand: "Evidence says traffic." And it was traffic. He came in grumbling about a lorry. Dr Kulkarni says I'm rewriting the rulebook my childhood gave me, where promises broke all the time. It's slow. But tonight I just said "Chai?" instead of crying.
Aadhya

qa.q: What did Aadhya feel when Mohit was late, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Aadhya felt a cold drop of fear and began thinking Mohit was bored or had found someone better.

qa.q: What turning point helped Aadhya stay calm?
qa.a: Aadhya remembered eight months of Mohit turning up and wrote "Evidence says traffic", using his past reliability to check the old fear.

qa.q: How might Mohit experience Aadhya's simple "Chai?" compared with the old spiral?
qa.a: He probably feels relaxed and trusted rather than accused, which makes being late less stressful for him.

grounding: A young adult with an unreliable childhood uses a partner's steady track record and therapy to calm an old fear of abandonment.

passage:
Pooja: are you free? had a weird moment
Simran: always. what happened
Pooja: my manager said "let's talk tomorrow" and I started packing my desk in my head
Simran: the classic
Pooja: but then I did the thing we practise. what's the evidence
Simran: and?
Pooja: last three reviews were good. she smiled when she said it
Simran: look at you 🤍
Pooja: a year ago I'd have messaged you twenty times tonight
Simran: you would've. and I'd still have answered every one
Pooja: I know. that's kind of why it's easier now
Pooja: remember when I was sure you'd drop me after I missed your birthday?
Simran: and I just moved the cake to Sunday
Pooja: still here
Simran: still here

qa.q: What did Pooja first feel when the manager said that?
qa.a: Pooja felt anxious, sure of being let go, and started mentally packing the desk right away.

qa.q: What choice did Pooja make instead of spiralling, and why did it help?
qa.a: Pooja checked the evidence, three good reviews and a smile, which calmed the fear with facts.

qa.q: How might Simran feel reading "that's kind of why it's easier now"?
qa.a: Simran may feel moved and quietly proud, seeing that being reliably there has helped Pooja trust more.

grounding: Two friends' chat shows how a friend's repeated reliability and practised reflection have made one of them more secure.
